questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The fact that Australia is an English speaking country, interesting courses at university, and personal wishes to explore the nature and wildlife in the brisbane area.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was difficult and expensive to find accommodation, but everything else exceeded my expectations.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. Of course everthing was new and overwhelming, but UQ did a great job with providing information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: E-mails, online and in-person meetings, and the possibility to ask at Student Central, which was a life-saver.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. I ended up using AirBnB but I would not recommend that.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Check bus connections beforehand.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is impossible for most students to afford the colleges.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Long but very well explained. Though it took a long time to get a reply from the administration.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A thorough guide, emails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start early.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was in my third year BA but took first and second year courses at UQ because it was in a field a little different from my usual one.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite different in some ways. There are a lot more assesments throughout the semester instead of one big exam at the end.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Psychological Research Methodology I (PSYC1040)
Introduction to Music Psychology (MUSC1300)
Music, Wellbeing and Health (MUSC2310)
Positive Psychology (PSYC2381)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Positive Psychology was by far my favorite course. So interesting and engaging with amazing tutors and professors. But I would recommend all my courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The student visa is very expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing and groceries were more expensive than I thought. Public transport was cheap. It's free to enter most nationalparks and nature areas.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Social clubs for everything you could ever want. All types of sport, crafts, music and so on.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: UQ Voices choir for international students. No music experience needed but a very welcoming group and great place to meet friends. The clubs and societies in general. You can absolutely find something within your interests.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: North Stradbroke Island, Moreton Island, Gold Coast hinterland, the list for amazing nature and wildlife experiences is never ending. In Brisbane the South Bank area is nice, Kangaroo Point, West End and the botanical gardens.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. Australians are very welcoming, and there are also a lot of international students, so you absolutely won't feel like an outsider.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs and societies.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Everything closes very early.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That it's so multicultural, people are generally very open and funny. And the culture around being in nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Use sunscreen, join clubs at uni and don't worry if everything seems overwhelming in the first few weeks. It will get better.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find a place with air condition!!!! Consider renting an e-bike or something similar. Public transport is NOT as good as in Europe.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting out of my comfort zone and exploring a new part of the world, making great friends along the way

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Honestly staying in a place without AC during the summer. And also feeling a bit lonely during the first two months. Remember to stay in touch with your friends and family at home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
